newsitem.title: USA: Bay State customer choice allowed to expand.
newsitem.headline: Bay State customer choice allowed to expand.

text.p: Bay State Gas Co said regulators approved expansion of its pilot program allowing residential and small commercial and industrial customers to select their natural gas supplier.
The company said it expects competition to dramatically accelerate system growth in one of the most undersaturated systems in the country.

The utility also reported third quarter, ended June 30, earnings of $0.45 per share including a gain of $0.58 per share from the sale of its MASSPOWER stake. Excluding the gain, the company had a loss per share of $0.13.
This compared with a $0.22 loss in 1996.

For the year to date, earnings per share excluding the gain were $2.55 compared to $2.60. Adjusted for this year's 4.8 percent warmer weather, earnings were $2.64 per share up from $2.44 in 1996's first nine months.
"We're encouraged by the underlying growth in earnings, said Chief Financial Officer Thomas Sherman.
In addition to sale of the MASSPOWER stake, he noted, the company also completed a sale-leaseback of its corporat office and sold its one-thired interest in KBC Energy Services.

The company also noted previous expectations its start up of its EnergyUSA unit would cost $0.07 to $0.12 per share this year, adding "our current expectations are more positive, and we expect results in the lower end of that range."

When Bay State's customer choice pilot was launched nearly a year ago, it was the first of its kind in New England. Customers participating in that pilot saved between 5 and 18 percent on their annual gas bills, the company said.
After evaluating the pilot's success in attracting almost 6,500 Springfield-area participants, the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities approved expansion of the plan.
This will extend eligibility to all of Bay State's customers in its Western Massachusetts service area.

In addition, small business customers in the Southeastern Massachusetts area will be eligible for the first time to participate in the program. As well as expanded eligibility, the second year of the pilot will include new features:
--Customers will be allowed to enroll throughout the program; last year the enrollment "window" was only 60 days;
--Customers will be able to change suppliers;
--Bay State has made gas storage capacity available to marketers on a voluntary basis and enhanced supplemental supply services to participating marketers; and
--Bay State and retail energy marketers will be conducting joint marketing programs to learn more about how to work together to better serve customers and attract new customers.
"We operate in one of the most undersaturated regions of the country, which is a result of the historical lack of gas delivery capability." President Joel Singer said.
"With the numerous gas supply projects being developed for the region, there is no reason why New England cannot achieve the same saturation levels as other regions of the country."
